ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, ABCE is a square, A is at the lower left, B is at the lower right, C is at the upper right, and E is at the upper left. Above side CE there is an equilateral triangle CDE, with vertex D above CE. On side BC there is an equilateral triangle BCF, with vertex F inside the square, to the left of BC. Reasoning: Since AB=1 and ABCE is a square, each side length of the square is 1. Using the coordinate method, set A=(0,0), B=(1,0), C=(1,1), E=(0,1). Equilateral triangle CDE has horizontal side CE as its base, with the vertex above, so D=(1/2, 1+sqrt(3)/2). Equilateral triangle BCF has vertical side BC as a side, with the vertex inside the square, namely to the left of BC, so F=(1-sqrt(3)/2, 1/2). Thus the difference in x-coordinates of FD is 1/2-(1-sqrt(3)/2)=(sqrt(3)-1)/2, and the difference in y-coordinates is 1+sqrt(3)/2-1/2=(sqrt(3)+1)/2. Therefore FD^2=((sqrt(3)-1)/2)^2+((sqrt(3)+1)/2)^2=2, so FD=sqrt(2).

method.method_draft: Use coordinates. From the text, ABCE is a square, CDE and BCF are equilateral, and AB=1, so every square side is 1. Set A=(0,0), B=(1,0), C=(1,1), E=(0,1). The equilateral triangle on horizontal segment CE has apex D=(1/2,1+sqrt(3)/2). The equilateral triangle on vertical segment BC with apex inside the square has F=(1-sqrt(3)/2,1/2). Then compute FD by the distance formula: the coordinate differences are ((sqrt(3)-1)/2,(sqrt(3)+1)/2), whose squared length is 2, so FD=sqrt(2).

method.method_draft: Use angle chasing and the Law of Cosines/Pythagorean theorem. From the image, focus on triangle DCF: D and F are the two equilateral-triangle vertices connected to C, with D above CE and F inside the square near the left of BC. From the text, CE=BC=AB=1 because ABCE is a square, and CD=CE=1 while CF=CB=1 because CDE and BCF are equilateral. At C, CD makes a 60° angle with CE, and CF makes a 60° angle with CB. Since CE is perpendicular to CB in the square, the visual placements put CD and CF on opposite sides around C so that angle DCF = 60° + 90° - 60°? More directly, CD is 60° above the leftward horizontal direction and CF is 60° from the downward vertical direction toward the left, giving a 90° angle between CD and CF. Thus triangle DCF has legs CD=CF=1 with included angle 90°, so FD=sqrt(1^2+1^2)=sqrt(2).
